correctness.rationale: All quantitative formulas are derived under the explicit unnormalized finite-field conventions. Planarity gives one overlap for every nonvertical shift; an exact orthogonality calculation gives the zero-shift magnitudes. The Weyl Fourier identity yields the full spectrum, and the zero set specifies the entire kernel by displacements. For rank-one differences, cross-fibre outer products plus constant-in-fibre diagonals force the exact three/two/one-fibre alternatives. The two-fibre swap is proved in both directions. The included checker has actually executed for q=3,5,7, including all 81 lifting singular values for q=3; those are finite corroboration only. Bounds: q odd prime powers >=3; all planar f; all q^4 Gabor shifts.

value.rationale: Planar-function graphs are canonical forbidden-subgroup relative difference sets. Their Gabor intensity measurements have a large linear kernel, but the complete nonlinear phase-orbit classification shows almost all structurally diverse signals recoverable and identifies the exact exceptional one-/two-fibre configurations. The precise two-fibre amplitude exchange and support-free uniqueness for fibre-sparse signals are natural mathematical conclusions about this window class, not routine numeric refinements or mere reparametrizations.
